perf.summary: Open-addressing probe recomputes (idx+i)%cap every iteration; replace modulo with an incrementing index that wraps by subtraction.
perf.currentCost: Inner loop executes `int c=(idx+i)%cap` each probe — an integer division/remainder (10-40 cycles on many targets, not vectorizable) on every step of a linear probe.
perf.proposedChange: Compute idx once, then iterate: `int c=idx; for(int i=0;i<cap;i++){ ... if(occ[c]==0)return false; if(CompareKeys...){...} c++; if(c==cap)c-=cap; }`. The wrap is a single compare+subtract, no division.
perf.rationale: Removes one integer remainder per probe iteration, replacing ~20-cycle div with a 1-cycle predictable compare/sub. Linear probing already walks contiguous memory; the branch `c==cap` is taken at most once per full scan so prediction is near-perfect.
perf.risk: None semantically: idx is already in [0,cap), and c increments by 1 each step wrapping at cap, producing the exact same probe sequence (idx, idx+1, ..., mod cap). cap must be >0 (already required for the original % cap).

perf.summary: Initial bucket uses signed `h % cap`; the masked-positive hash means an unsigned reduction is valid and avoids signed-remainder overhead.
perf.currentCost: `int idx = h % cap` is a signed remainder; signed % emits extra instructions to handle the sign of the dividend even though h is already non-negative (GetUnmanagedHash returns h & 0x7FFFFFFF).
perf.proposedChange: Use `int idx = (int)((uint)h % (uint)cap);` so the JIT/Burst emits an unsigned remainder, or if cap is constrained to a power of two by the caller, expose a masked variant `idx = h & (cap-1)`.
perf.rationale: h is guaranteed in [0, 2^31-1], so unsigned reduction is identical in value but the codegen for unsigned % is cheaper (no sign-correction). A power-of-two mask path would strength-reduce the only remaining division entirely.
perf.risk: Value-identical because h>=0 and cap>0, so signed and unsigned remainder agree. The mask variant is only valid when cap is a power of two — gate it behind a separate method or a documented precondition; do not silently apply.

perf.summary: Byte-by-byte hash and compare defeat vectorization for common blittable key sizes (4/8/16 bytes); special-case word-sized keys.
perf.currentCost: Both loops iterate sizeof(T) times one byte at a time. For a 16-byte key that is 16 load+branch iterations for compare and 16 mul-add iterations for hash, far more than the data warrants; the per-byte loop is a serial dependency chain (h=h*31+p[i]) that Burst cannot SIMD.
perf.proposedChange: Branch on sizeof(T): for sizeof(T)==4 compare/hash via *(uint*)a; for ==8 via *(ulong*); for ==16 via two ulongs. CompareKeys becomes a single (or two) word comparisons; hashing can mix words with a multiply-xor finalizer. Fall back to the byte loop for odd sizes. Since sizeof(T) is a JIT-time constant per generic instantiation, Burst will dead-code-eliminate the wrong branches.
perf.rationale: Word-wide loads cut the compare from N byte-loads to N/8 word-loads and remove the per-byte branch; the equality early-out on mismatch is rarely hit for full-key compares anyway. Fewer loads, shorter dependency chain, better for Burst which specializes per generic type.
perf.risk: Hash VALUE will differ from the current byte-polynomial hash. That is acceptable only if no external contract depends on the exact hash value (it is an internal probe index). The compare must remain a full bitwise equality (same observable result). Unaligned word loads are fine on the supported targets but note it for strict-alignment platforms; CompareKeys result is bit-identical so observable behavior of QueryCacheGet is preserved.

perf.summary: qt/2 is recomputed repeatedly inside FindBestCentroid's nested loops; hoist the half-size and reuse.
perf.currentCost: FindBestCentroid evaluates `qt/2` once per outer node for the `ok` test and again per incident edge in the inner condition `sz[v] > qt/2`. qt is loop-invariant for the whole call, so this is a redundant signed division (qt/2) executed O(edges) times.
perf.proposedChange: At the top of FindBestCentroid compute `int half = qt >> 1;` (qt is the queue tail count, always >=0, so arithmetic shift == /2) and use `half` in both the outer and inner comparisons.
perf.rationale: Removes a division (or at least a redundant recompute) from the innermost edge-scan loop, replacing it with a single hoisted shift. The centroid scan touches every edge of the component, so this is the hot inner loop of each decomposition level.
perf.risk: None: qt is a count of enqueued nodes, strictly >=0, so qt>>1 equals qt/2 exactly. Pure hoist, no behavior change.

perf.summary: FindBestCentroid re-scans every node's edges to validate the centroid, an O(V+E) pass that duplicates information already derivable from subtree sizes in O(V).
perf.currentCost: After ComputeSubtreeSizes, FindBestCentroid does a second full edge walk per candidate to find the max child subtree, making centroid finding O(V+E) with an extra adjacency traversal each decomposition level.
perf.proposedChange: During the reverse pass in ComputeSubtreeSizes, also accumulate per-node maxChildSize[u] (the largest sz over children) by updating maxChildSize[p]=max(maxChildSize[p], sz[u]). Then the centroid test is purely sz-based: node u is a centroid iff max(maxChildSize[u], qt - sz[u]) <= qt/2, evaluated in a single O(V) forward scan with no adjacency walk.
perf.rationale: Eliminates the second adjacency traversal (the dominant edge-touching loop) and replaces it with an O(1) test per node using an array filled during the existing size pass — same total info, strictly fewer edge visits, lower constant and no extra asymptotic term beyond the unavoidable size computation.
perf.risk: Requires one more stackalloc int[numNodes] (maxChildSize), increasing stack working set by 4*numNodes bytes — acceptable given numNodes already drives several such buffers; on deeply recursive decomposition the stackalloc is per-call so verify total stack budget. The selected centroid is equivalent (same definition: no subtree, including the parent side qt-sz[u], exceeds qt/2). Init maxChildSize to 0 each level.

perf.summary: The `queue` scratch buffer duplicates traversal order that `parent` already encodes; but more concretely, removed[] init loop can be fused and buffers right-sized.
perf.currentCost: Four stackalloc int[numNodes] plus a byte[numNodes] are allocated every call; the removed[] zero-init is a separate loop from the others. On mobile with large numNodes this is a sizable per-call stack footprint and an extra init pass.
perf.proposedChange: Allocate the int buffers in one stackalloc int[numNodes*3] block and slice (sz/parent/queue) to improve locality, and zero removed[] with a single Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned/Burst memset rather than a scalar loop. Keep removed as the only persistent-across-iterations buffer.
perf.rationale: A single contiguous allocation improves cache locality and a vectorized memset clears removed[] faster than a scalar byte loop (which Burst may not auto-vectorize across the function boundary). Reduces setup overhead per outer decomposition call.
perf.risk: Pointer slicing must keep correct alignment (int* slices of an int block are naturally aligned). InitBlock semantics identical to the zero loop. Low impact; mainly setup-phase, not the inner loop.
